Host switching — UI prototypes

Features·budding·implemented·JUL 09, 2026

The host tab bar is a solid browser-tab metaphor, but it reads as a toolbar bolted above the canvas, switching is mouse-only, and it never leaves the tab-row box. This note renders the bar as it is, then pushes on two axes the first cut missed — visual craft (frosted glass, per-host hue, a seam that dissolves into the canvas, motion) and paradigm (the host as a coloured room; a zoom-out host map that rides kolu's canvas camera) — each as a faithful mockup grounded in the seams the code already exposes.

Kolu renders each host as a browser-style tab — click to switch, + to add over ssh, ✕ to drop. packages/client/src/host/HostSelectorStrip.tsx It’s a good start: the metaphor needs no manual, health is legible before you switch, and the strip degrades to an overflow menu as it narrows. But it’s stuck on two axes. It looks like a toolbar bolted above the canvas — hard borders, flat fills, an opaque band with a seam. And it never leaves the tab-row box: every idea is still “a row of tabs.” This note fixes the first cut on both — craft, then paradigm.

The bar today

Three hosts as tabs. Each carries a connection dot, the name, a fixed-width Padi · Kaval slot (so a sick remote shows red before you switch), an optional amber awaiting count, and — for guests — a remove ✕. A click writes activeHost and the canvas re-keys; no reload.The switch is a synchronous signal write — setActiveHost(props.host) in packages/client/src/host/HostSelectorStrip.tsx; useEntry(activeHost) re-keys the per-host canvas. Nothing reflows because every tab reserves the same daemon-slot width whether active or not.

Kolu [pureintent] — Kolu [srid@zest]
localP>_srid@zestP>_✕sincereintent2P>_✕+

Faithful to the shipped strip. Health reads well — the green dots and the amber 2 say sincereintent has agents waiting. But look at the seam: a hard opaque band with a 1px border sits on top of the canvas grid, not part of it.

Three problems the first cut left standing:

  • It reads as a toolbar, not part of the workspace. Opaque fill, hard border, a visible seam against the canvas. Nothing about it says “this is the canvas’s frame.”
  • It never leaves the tab-row box. Every host is a rectangle in a row; add enough and it overflows into a ⋯ menu. The row is the ceiling.
  • Switching is mouse-only, and the keyboard tier is taken. ⌘1–9 is positional terminal switch, Ctrl+Tab cycles terminals, ⌘T/⌘N make one — hosts get nothing.Confirmed in packages/client/src/input/actions.ts: the switchTo1…9 block binds { key: String(i), mod: true } to dock-row terminal switch, and Ctrl+Tab (shiftOptional) cycles terminals. The palette (packages/client/src/commands.tsx) registers no host action. So a host keyboard path can’t borrow the number row — that tier belongs to terminals.

Make the box beautiful

Before changing the paradigm, fix the craft — same tab metaphor, but it stops looking bolted-on. Four moves: frost the band so the canvas grid shows through (it becomes a lens over the workspace, not a lid); give each host its own hue — a coloured focus ring on the dot and, on the active tab, a soft hue underglow — so a host feels like a place, not a label; dissolve the seam by letting the active tab’s belly bleed into the canvas (the connected-tab metaphor done right — no border line between “active host” and “its canvas”); and cross-fade on switch (150 ms hue + belly slide) so hopping hosts feels like moving, not repainting.

localsrid@zestP>_✕sincereintent2+

Same tabs, real craft. The band is frosted glass — the grid reads straight through it. Each host owns a hue (slate · violet · teal); the active tab glows in its hue and its belly dissolves into the canvas — no seam. A switch cross-fades the hue and slides the belly. Resting tabs are quiet; the active one is rich.

The hue already exists — we're just spending it better

Kolu already derives a per-hostname theme colour and tints the window chrome with it (themeColor() in packages/client/src/ChromeBar.tsx, read off useServerIdentity). Today it’s a faint whole-bar wash. Promoting it to a per-host identity — one hue per tab, the active hue underglowing the belly — costs no new data, just a --hue custom property per chip. color-mix and backdrop-filter are the whole toolkit.

Out of the box · the host as a room

Now leave the row. A host isn’t a document you tab between — it’s a place you’re inside. So drop the tab strip and let the active host own the whole window: its hue washes the canvas edges in a soft halo, and identity collapses to one thing — a presence pill floating at the top (“you are in srid@zest”). Click it (or ⌘K) and it blooms into a vertical list of rooms, each in its own hue, that you teleport between with a full-window hue cross-fade. No row to overflow: ten hosts is a scroll, not a ⋯ menu.

srid@zest▾
local
srid@zest
sincereintent2

The active host is the environment — a violet halo bleeds in from the top edge, so you always feel where you are without reading a label. Identity is one presence pill; clicking it blooms the room list. Switching cross-fades the whole halo to the next hue. This is the strongest “fit with the canvas” answer: the host isn’t chrome above the canvas, it tints the canvas.

The trade: with no persistent row, a sick remote can’t shout from the corner of your eye — you’d learn it’s red only on opening the bloom.Mitigation, and the reason the “room” and the “orb rail” pair: keep a thin vertical rail of host coins (each host’s hue, pulsing amber when it’s awaiting you) flush against the canvas edge as the room’s resting state. It’s the ambient-attention channel the pill alone lacks — the pill answers “where am I,” the rail answers “who needs me,” and clicking either opens the same bloom.

Out of the box · the host map

The second paradigm leans all the way into what kolu already is: an infinite canvas with a camera per host. So make switching navigation of one continuous space. ⌘K (or a pinch/zoom-out past the canvas edge) pulls the camera back to a host map — every host a live-preview card of its real tiles in miniature, laid out spatially, the active one lifted, an awaiting one glowing amber. Pick one and the camera flies in. Switching stops being “click a tab” and becomes “fly to a place.”

local
srid@zest
sincereintent2

Zoom out and every host is a live thumbnail of its actual canvas — you recognize a machine by what’s on it, not a name string. The active card is lifted in its hue; sincereintent glows amber because it’s waiting. Click → the camera flies in. Reuses kolu’s per-host canvas + camera (cameraSwap, useCanvasViewport) rather than inventing chrome.

Why this one is deeply kolu-native

Kolu already keeps a per-host canvas and a camera it swaps on switch (packages/client/src/canvas/cameraSwap.ts, packages/client/src/canvas/viewport/useCanvasViewport.ts). The host map isn’t a new surface — it’s the zoomed-out state of the space that’s already there. The live thumbnails are the same tile tree the canvas renders, drawn small. The cost is a real-preview render at map scale; the payoff is that “switch host” and “navigate the canvas” become one gesture, not two mental models.

The interaction underneath

Whatever the surface — polished tabs, room bloom, or host map — the keyboard story is the same, and it isn’t a new invention: kolu already ships this exact pattern for workspaces. ⌘⇧K opens the workspace switcher, which is literally commandPalette.openGroup("Search workspaces") packages/client/src/useActionContext.ts — a scoped palette group, not a bespoke modal. Host switching mirrors it one-for-one: ⌘⇧H (H for host) → commandPalette.openGroup("Switch host"), fuzzy-matched and sorted by who’s awaiting you; Enter picks. ⌘⇧H is free and follows the Mod+Shift+<letter> convention the codebase already names for exactly this.packages/client/src/input/actions.ts line 281 calls out “the Mod+Shift+<letter> convention used by openWorkspaceSwitcher,” and a grep confirms no KeyH / ⌘⇧H binding exists in actions.ts or prohibitedKeybinds.ts. So host switching gets a chord that’s free, precedented, and mnemonic — no invented combo, no hedge.

⌘⇧H → type → ↵ — the same switcher pattern as ⌘⇧K workspaces, just a different group. Awaiting hosts float to a Needs you group; the fuzzy match bolds the hit (z → srid@zest). No per-host number caps — those chords are terminals’. It’s additive to the palette, so there’s almost no new UI to build.

And one smaller fix worth pairing anywhere: the + should autocomplete from ~/.ssh/config and recents with a live reachability dot, instead of a blank field you type into from memory — and the destructive ✕ should leave the resting surface for a right-click / overflow action.

+srid@zest
srid@zestrecent
srid@pu-boxssh config
root@fly-edgessh config
The + completes as you type — ~/.ssh/config entries and recents, each with a reachability dot (grey = untried). No memorized host string, no blind ssh.

What I’d ship, and where it wires in

The moves stack, they don’t compete. Ship the craft first (§2) — frosted band, per-host hue, seam dissolve, cross-fade — because it’s pure CSS on the strip that exists and it makes every later paradigm look right. Then the palette switcher (§5) for the keyboard win. The two paradigms are bigger bets: the host map (§4) is the one I’d chase, because it’s not new chrome — it’s the zoomed-out state of a canvas kolu already has, so it earns its complexity. The room (§3) is the boldest visual but the riskiest (it removes the always-visible attention channel; it needs the orb rail to be honest). None of it invents host state: the switch stays one activeHost write, and the host list + urgency counts already stream into the strip.

Status — the craft pass shipped

The craft pass (§2) shipped in #1743: per-host identity hue on the tabs and a faint wash across the canvas floor, a neutral borderless header, the seam dissolve, the daemon glyphs quieting at rest, a dots grid, and a house glyph disambiguating the local host. That PR also ungated remote hosts (the “+” is always present, alpha-warned at point of use) and added keyboard switching — though the shipped chord is a direct Ctrl+Cmd+N host-cycle, not the ⌘⇧H palette switcher this note proposed; the switcher and the two paradigms (the room §3, the host map §4) remain open directions. The hue derivation landed as the shared packages/common/src/hostHue.ts the PWA theme-color also draws from.
